h1: The 8 Best Microwaves for Dorm Rooms of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Microwaves for Dorm Rooms: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 compact microwaves for dorm rooms compared on 700W output, mute buttons, presets and footprint, from COMFEE' to Toshiba.
summary: The COMFEE' 0.7 cu ft microwave is the dorm default: 700W, a mute function for late-night reheats and a small footprint. If you want simpler controls, the Chefman 0.7 has six labeled presets. On a tight budget, the Farberware is the cheapest here. Only the Toshiba goes to 900W and 0.9 cu ft, so confirm your housing rules before buying it.
intro: A dorm microwave has to clear three bars at once: fit a shelf or fridge top, stay under whatever wattage your housing office allows and not wake a roommate at 1 a.m. Many cheap microwaves forget the last one, and the listing rarely mentions it.

We reviewed eight compact models, seven at 0.7 cubic feet and 700W and one larger 900W unit. Each was ranked on footprint, wattage, mute and safety features and how simple the controls are. Housing rules vary, so wattage limits are a check you should run yourself.

products.name: COMFEE' Countertop Microwave Oven (0.7 Cu.Ft, Standard)
products.verdict: 700W, a mute function and ECO mode in a small body. The easiest dorm pick.
products.description:
This COMFEE' is a 0.7 cu ft, 700W microwave with an ECO mode and a mute function so a midnight reheat will not beep a sleeping roommate awake. It is compact enough to move in and out each semester.

It wins because it covers all the dorm basics for a modest price. Against the Pearl White version it costs less for identical specs, and against the Chefman it has a plainer control panel.

Buy it for a standard dorm. Check your wattage limit anyway.
products.idealFor: Students who want a no-fuss dorm microwave.

products.name: Chefman Countertop Microwave Oven 0.7 Cu. Ft.
products.verdict: 700W with ten power levels, six food presets, a child lock and a mute button.
products.description:
The Chefman 0.7 offers 700 watts with 10 power levels, six presets labeled by food, an eco mode, a child safety lock and a mute button. It has a compact footprint for a desk or shelf.

It ranks just behind the COMFEE' because it costs about the same and the extra presets are a convenience. It beats the Chefman Compact with more presets.

A fine first microwave for a new student.

products.name: Farberware 0.7 Cu. Ft. Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: The least expensive pick, with 700W, auto cook settings and multi-stage cooking.
products.description:
The Farberware is the least expensive pick here, with 700 watts, auto cook settings, defrost, an easy-clean interior, a child safety lock and multi-stage cooking that chains a defrost cycle into a cook cycle.

It ranks third because it lacks a mute function in the listing. It beats the Frigidaire on price.

Buy it if budget is the main limit.

products.name: FRIGIDAIRE EMW733BLACKAMZ 0.7 Cu. Ft. Microwave
products.verdict: A delayed start and two defrost timers in a 700W body.
products.description:
The Frigidaire has a delayed start that lets you queue a cook cycle to begin later, two defrost timers instead of one catch-all button, and 700W output.

It ranks fourth because the delayed start is a niche feature and the listing leaves out a mute button. It gives more control than the Farberware.

Useful if your class schedule is irregular.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER Countertop Microwave Oven 0.7 Cu.Ft, 700W
products.verdict: A fingerprint-resistant black finish and multi-stage cooking at 700W.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER lists a fingerprint-resistant black finish that holds up to shared use, multi-stage cooking that chains defrost into reheat, a child safety lock and 700W output.

It ranks fifth because it lacks a mute function. It looks cleaner than the white models.

A good fit for a shared suite.

products.name: Chefman Compact Countertop Microwave Oven 0.7 Cu. Ft.
products.verdict: Three focused presets, 10 power levels and a mute button. Simple for roommates.
products.description:
The Chefman Compact lists 700W with 10 power levels, two defrost settings, three focused presets, a child safety lock and a mute button.

It ranks sixth because the other Chefman has more presets. The panel is plain enough that a new roommate can use it on the first try.

A fit if you share a microwave.
cons: Fewer presets than the other Chefman

products.name: COMFEE' Countertop Microwave Oven (Pearl White)
products.verdict: The same COMFEE' in pearl white, at a higher price.
products.description:
This COMFEE' has the same mute function, ECO mode and 700W output as the standard model, in a pearl white finish and a compact footprint.

It ranks seventh because it costs more for the same specs. The finish is the only difference.

Pick it only if you want white to match your room.
cons: Costs more for the same specs

products.name: TOSHIBA Microwave Oven (0.9 Cu.Ft, 900W)
products.verdict: 900W, a 0.9 cu ft cavity and 11 power levels. Faster, but check your dorm rules.
products.description:
The Toshiba lists 900W output, which heats faster than the 700W picks, a 0.9 cu ft cavity larger than most here and 11 power levels.

It ranks last because 900W may exceed a dorm's wattage limit and the cavity needs more room. It is the best choice for an off-campus apartment.

Buy it if your housing allows it. Otherwise take a 700W pick.
cons: May exceed a dorm wattage limit
products.idealFor: Off-campus apartments and suites with no limit.

whatMatters.detail: Many housing offices cap appliance wattage, and 700W is a common ceiling. Look up your dorm's rule before buying, because a 900W unit may be banned. If the policy is silent, ask the housing office.
A 0.7 cu ft microwave is compact but still needs about 18 inches of width and ventilation space. Measure your shelf or fridge top, and leave a few inches behind and above for airflow.
Beeps carry through thin walls. A mute button silences them, and several models list one, including the COMFEE' and both Chefman units. Check for it on the listing.
In a shared room, nobody reads the manual. Labeled presets and a few clear buttons beat a complicated panel. A child safety lock also stops accidental starts.

whatMatters.factor: Check the cavity against your plate
whatMatters.detail: A 0.7 cu ft cavity fits a standard plate, but large bowls can be tight. If you reheat big meals, consider a bigger cavity, as long as your housing rules allow it.

faq.q: What wattage is allowed in a dorm?
faq.a: It varies by school, and 700W is a common limit. Check your housing rules before buying.
For reheating and plates, yes. A 0.9 cu ft unit like the Toshiba gives more room.

faq.q: Which microwave has a mute button?
faq.a: The COMFEE' units and both Chefman microwaves list one.

faq.q: Is the Pearl White COMFEE' worth the extra?
faq.a: Only for the color. The specs match the standard model.

faq.q: Can I use a 900W microwave in a dorm?
faq.a: Maybe, but many dorms cap wattage. Ask your housing office before buying the Toshiba.

faq.q: Do I need a child lock?
faq.a: It stops accidental starts in a shared room. Both Chefman models and the Farberware list one.

finalTake: For most dorms the COMFEE' 0.7 cu ft microwave is the right answer: 700W, a mute function and a small footprint. For simpler shared use, the Chefman 0.7 has six labeled presets. On a tight budget, the Farberware is the cheapest. The Toshiba 900W only makes sense if your housing allows it.
